rule.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement and Permissible Grounds
rule.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] A landlord evicting a tenant from a covered rental unit must have one of 17 enumerated 'just cause' reasons under Ordinance Section 37.9(a) as the dominant motive for the eviction, and mere lease expiration or ownership change does not constitute just cause. Permissible reasons include tenant fault grounds (such as non-payment, substantial lease breach, severe nuisance, illegal use, refusal to execute lease extension, refusal of lawful access, or unapproved subtenant) and specified no-fault grounds (such as owner/family occupancy, condo conversion sale, demolition, capital improvement, substantial rehabilitation, Ellis Act withdrawal, lead remediation, development agreement, expired Good Samaritan tenancy, or Planning Code Section 317 demolition).
rule.coverage_conditions: Just cause eviction protections apply to rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including units exempt from rent increase limitations such as post-June 13, 1979 new construction, Costa-Hawkins eligible units, and certain units regulated by another government agency. [Ordinance Section 37.9]
